description: KAMP (Klimatilpasning- og Arealanvendelsesværktøj til Miljø- og Planmedarbejdere) is a national map tool from the Danish Environmental Protection Agency that helps municipal environment and planning staff screen areas for climate adaptation. The tool read on 2026-09-28 shows land data layers for hydrology (watercourse centrelines, catchments, flow paths and a screening of buildings exposed to near-surface groundwater), coastal protection structures, chronic and acute coastal erosion, protected nature and Natura 2000 areas, soil contamination, carbon-rich lowland soils, adopted and proposed local plans, sewer catchment plans and municipal plan frames, municipal plans for flooding and erosion, buildings that have received damage compensation, cadastral parcels and historical maps, with impact tabs for precipitation, watercourses, groundwater and the sea; users can generate a report or download a QGIS project. Coverage is Denmark. Access is free in the browser; the licence of the layers is not stated in the tool. Caveats: layers come from many agencies with their own dates, and the impact scenarios were not opened. It supports flood and groundwater hazard exposure screening of buildings, drainage and coastal defences. Related record: data-denmark-high-water-statistics-2024 complements it with extreme sea level statistics.
